title: Floating point formats
blurb: Every format a modern accelerator will multiply for you, and what each one gives up.
note: Exponent bits buy range and mantissa bits buy precision, and every format here is a different answer to which of the two you can afford to lose. Energy per multiply falls roughly with the square of the mantissa width, which is why the list keeps getting shorter.

sources.title: FP8 Formats for Deep Learning, arXiv 2209.05433

rows.name: fp64
rows.use: Scientific work where the answer must survive the arithmetic

rows.name: fp32
rows.use: The default everywhere until accelerators changed the economics

rows.name: tf32
rows.use: fp32's range with fp16's precision, on tensor cores

detail.summary: Not a storage format. It is what a tensor core does to fp32 inputs.

rows.name: bf16
rows.use: Training, because keeping fp32's range matters more than precision

detail.summary: Chops fp32's mantissa and keeps its exponent, so conversion is a truncation.

rows.name: fp16
rows.use: Inference and older training, with loss scaling to avoid underflow

detail.summary: No infinities, which is how it reaches 448 rather than 240.

rows.name: fp8 E5M2
rows.use: Gradients, where range matters more than precision

rows.name: fp4 E2M1
rows.use: Blackwell tensor cores, with a shared scale per block

detail.summary: Sixteen values in total, and 3.6 binades of range. It only works with block scaling.
